title: Beyond Structure-Driven Tuning: Cost-Aligned Graph Optimization for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search

problem.claim: Graph-based approximate nearest neighbor search can suffer from redundant distance evaluations and inefficient traversal behavior that hinder high-recall performance.

gap.claim: Structure-driven graph construction and tuning may not reflect actual search traversal dynamics because geometric proximity is only an indirect proxy for search efficiency.

contributions.claim: PIGR is a trace-driven framework that aligns graph-search efficiency with observed search behavior.
PIGR analyzes self-query search traces and applies trace-guided, budgeted prune-and-add edge edits without modifying the deployed search procedure.
PIGR operates as a post-construction plug-in for optimizing deployed indexes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report 1.3x–2.5x speedups at near-exact recall across diverse datasets and index families.
The authors report that PIGR consistently outperforms the best build-time tuned baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: ANNS is widely used in vector databases and retrieval systems.
Existing structure-driven construction and tuning can produce static graphs that fail to reflect traversal dynamics, causing redundant evaluations and reduced high-recall efficiency.
PIGR uses self-query traces to identify inefficient traversal behavior and iteratively optimize the index through budgeted edge edits without changing the search procedure.
The authors report 1.3x–2.5x speedups at near-exact recall and consistent gains over build-time tuned baselines.

source_observation.claim: Observed search traces can reveal low-yield expansions and local detours that static graph structure does not capture.

interpretation.claim: Optimization objectives may be better aligned with runtime behavior than with geometric or structural proxies alone.

application.claim: Post-construction, trace-guided graph edits could improve retrieval efficiency while preserving the deployed search procedure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported gains generalize beyond the evaluated datasets and index families.

unknowns: Specific datasets, index families, baselines, and evaluation settings are not provided.
The abstract does not specify the recall metric definition or runtime measurement conditions.
The mechanism for selecting prune-and-add edge edits and their budget is not detailed.
